title: Working at Stillwell's Hotel while pregnant and going into early labor
summary: Working six nights a week at downtown Stillwell's Hotel with Ben Borders's group, she shopped for the baby and began labor two and a half months early.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Talking about my children and grandchildren

blocks.x: And your son, you told me on the tape we did over, but we didn't repeat it, he was born at 6-1/2 months and he weighed 2-1/4 pounds.
That is right, yes, indeed. He certainly was. Well, he was a 6-1/2 months baby. And I was working with a group -- did I tell you this on the other tape, about
the group I was working with at that time?
I was working at a -- I thought I said this, but anyhow, I was working at a hotel downtown called Stillwell's.
Yeah, I think you did on the other tape, but we don't have it on this tape.
Oh, we don't. Well, anyway, it was at Stillwell's Hotel, this was a popular hotel downtown. It's either on Spring -- it's Main or Spring Street.
I've seen the sign. The hotel is still there.

Right. Well, I guess it's still there. And it was an old hotel then. You know, it had been a very prominent hotel at that time. I don't say it was as prominent as the Biltmore, but I guess you would call it about a second or third rate hotel, and it had music, and I was working with a little group. Ben Borders was the drummer and leader, and then Jim Wynn, who became very well known, and who passed on about a year and a half ago, a saxophone player. And there was another -- let me see, there was a trumpet player, Cortland Mason, and myself. There were four of us working this job. And my husband at that time worked at the Carthay Circle

Theater, he was a doorman there and doing other little jobs around. So we had decided that I was going to work about two more weeks and then take off and get ready for the baby, you know. And we were both anxiously awaiting this baby. And lo and behold, one day I went shopping and my sister Florida who was living with my husband and I at that time, she hadn't been in California but about six months, but anyway, she went shopping with me and we were shopping for the baby, you know. So I was working six nights a week. I think I had had that -- yes, I had had that Sunday off, because this was on a Monday. So we went downtown and we went to about three or four stores, shopping for the baby, and my sister had a little job in the afternoon, where she worked afternoons, and I guess about 2:00 o'clock, or something like that, but she went on to her job. And then I continued to shop around, and then I journeyed back home. Well, on my way back home I began to feel pains, you know, in my stomach. Well, I wasn't even thinking about -- you know, I knew it wasn't time for the baby to come, two and a half months ahead of time. And I said, well, I guess I'd better go home. So I got on the bus -- no, was it a bus? A streetcar. We didn't even have busses then. A streetcar. Well, we lived on the east side, I think it was 29th Street. And I got on the streetcar and started back home, and I had to change. I think I changed -- did I change there? No, no. Because the way I was at the time, I just got on this streetcar and went

straight down Central Avenue. And as I got close to home, I just began to feel so terrible, and I said oh, my God, I hope I can make it home. So I got off the streetcar at my corner, you know, and walked on home, and I just barely made it. I was so happy to get home. And we lived upstairs in an apartment, and I went on upstairs and the first thing I did was sit on the side of the bed, and then I would lie down a little while, and then I'd sit up a little while, I'd lie down. Then I said well, I guess I'd better pull my clothes off. I pulled my clothes off. I just kept thinking I would feel better. Instead of feeling better I was feeling worse all the time.
